title: Pelvic pain in women: early pregnancy, torsion, bleeding cysts and pelvic sepsis
summary: A woman with pelvic pain has a short list of time-critical diagnoses. Learn a systematic transabdominal pelvic scan, the criteria for a definite intrauterine pregnancy, the signs of ectopic pregnancy and haemoperitoneum, why Doppler misleads in ovarian torsion, and how to separate a bleeding cyst from a tubo-ovarian abscess.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency, acute and urgent care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and physician associates who assess women with pelvic pain or bleeding in early pregnancy. It teaches transabdominal scanning only.
outcomes: Perform a systematic transabdominal scan of the uterus, adnexa, pouch of Douglas and Morison's pouch
Apply the criteria for a definite intrauterine pregnancy and separate a pseudosac from an early gestational sac
Recognise the signs of ectopic pregnancy and haemoperitoneum, and act on them
Recognise the features of ovarian torsion and explain why normal Doppler flow does not exclude it
Separate a haemorrhagic cyst from a tubo-ovarian abscess, and refer appropriately
references: Stein JC, et al. Emergency physician ultrasonography for evaluating patients at risk for ectopic pregnancy: a meta-analysis. Annals of Emergency Medicine. 2010;56:674-83.
